title: Occupancy and Residency Certification — Supporting Documents and Household Occupancy Requirements by Plan
content:
Each Occupancy and Residency Certification plan names the document that must be on file before a certification counts, how often that document is renewed, and which household members' occupancy the plan relies on.

## Supporting document on file

| Plan | Document that must be on file before the certification counts | Months after which it must be resubmitted |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Annual Certification | none | 0 (no document required) |
| Joint Borrower Certification | none | 0 (no document required) |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | marriage status attestation | 12 |
| Deferral Period Certification | evidence of the legal right to remain in the home | 12 |
| Living Trust Certification | certification of trust | 36 |
| Authorized Representative Certification | power of attorney or guardianship order | 24 |

## Household occupancy settings

| Plan | Eligible non-borrowing spouse must also occupy the home | Certification attests the non-borrowing spouse remained married to the borrower | Borrower who is a living-trust beneficiary must occupy the home |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Annual Certification | no | no | no |
| Joint Borrower Certification | no | no | no |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | yes | yes | no |
| Deferral Period Certification | yes | yes | no |
| Living Trust Certification | no | no | yes |
| Authorized Representative Certification | no | no | no |

## Settings common to every plan

The following hold identically under Standard Annual, Joint Borrower, Non-Borrowing Spouse Household, Deferral Period, Living Trust and Authorized Representative Certification:

- a caregiver or relative living in the home does **not** satisfy occupancy for the borrower;
- the borrower may **not** treat another home as principal residence for part of the year (no seasonal or second home);
- on a two-to-four-unit property the borrower **must** occupy one unit.

## Reading the tables

A plan with no supporting document has a renewal period of 0 months, because nothing is required. Where a document is required, it counts only while it is not older than the renewal period shown for that plan.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A certification of trust placed on file for a Living Trust Certification profile remains current for 36 months; a power of attorney on an Authorized Representative Certification profile, for 24 months; a marriage status attestation on a Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification profile, for 12 months.
